title: A tiled matrix multiply
hints: Five loops, outermost first: tile row `ib`, tile column `jb`, then `k`, then the rows `i` and columns `j` inside the tile.
Tile `(ib, jb)` covers rows `ib*th` to `ib*th + th - 1` and columns `jb*tw` to `jb*tw + tw - 1`.

The innermost line is the same as in the plain loops: add `a[i][k] * b[k][j]` onto `c[i][j]`. Because `k` counts up outside the two in-tile loops, every sum still gets its terms in the order `k = 0, 1, 2, ...`.

answer.code:
let matmul_tiled (a : float array array) (b : float array array) (th : int) (tw : int) : float array array =
  let n = Array.length a and p = Array.length b and m = Array.length b.(0) in
  let c = Array.make_matrix n m 0.0 in
  for ib = 0 to n / th - 1 do
    for jb = 0 to m / tw - 1 do
      for k = 0 to p - 1 do
        for i = ib * th to ib * th + th - 1 do
          for j = jb * tw to jb * tw + tw - 1 do
            c.(i).(j) <- c.(i).(j) +. a.(i).(k) *. b.(k).(j)
          done
        done
      done
    done
  done;
  c
answer.explain: The tile loops `ib` and `jb` pick a block of outputs. For each `k`, the two inner loops add one more term to every sum in the block. Each `c[i][j]` still receives its products in the order `k = 0, 1, 2, ...`, one add at a time, so the floats match the plain triple loop bit for bit. Only the order in which different outputs take their turns has changed.
